DI64 is a medical diagnosis code representing "stroke without mention of hemorrhage or infarction" (slagtilfælde uden oplysning om blødning eller infarkt) [^src1]. In the context of the Danish healthcare system's quality monitoring for [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]], DI64 plays a critical role in tracking patient outcomes and treatment safety [^src1]. Specifically, it is utilized alongside other codes to measure the incidence of [[iskaemisk-apopleksi|ischemic stroke]] among patients with atrial fibrillation, serving as an indicator of potentially insufficient anticoagulation therapy [^src4].

To calculate the incidence of ischemic stroke (Quality Indicator 5 in the national atrial fibrillation database), the [[landspatientregisteret|Danish National Patient Register]] is queried for specific diagnostic and procedural combinations [^src4]. The methodology incorporates DI64 alongside [[di63|DI63]] (cerebral infarction) and [[dz501|DZ501]] (contact for other physical therapy) combined with either DI63 or DI64 to comprehensively capture stroke events [^src1]. This approach allows the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to systematically evaluate whether patients are receiving adequate protective treatment against stroke, a primary complication of atrial fibrillation [^src3]. The consistent use of DI64 across multiple annual reports (2023–2025) underscores its importance as a standardized metric in Denmark's cardiovascular quality assurance infrastructure [^src5].
